model.name: Codex (GPT-5 family)
model.note: The requested GPT-5.6 Sol product label was not exposed by this session.

scope.purpose: Replace 29 independent dynamic far-star overlays with a bounded pattern baked only into generated/recycled background rows.

implementation.representation: 28-row deterministic baked pattern: one far point in every row and one additional point in pattern row zero
rowGenerationOrder: generate at most one near star
bake one or two far stars into an unoccupied cell
implementation.nearCollisionPolicy: Near wins. The far point uses one bounded +11 corridor or +17 full-width fallback; a generated row has at most one near point.
implementation.fighterColumns: interior columns 9-30, leaving hull/muzzle boundary cells untouched
implementation.twinkle: disabled; glyph variation is deterministic pattern data

visualModel.density: exactly 29 far points in every warmed 28-row period; positions may differ from the retired record population
ownerSmokeQuestions: Does the starfield still read as multilayered?
Do the far points look like intentional background rather than foreground attachments?
Do the existing brighter/larger near points provide enough motion and depth?
Is density acceptable through ring wrap and capital reconstruction?
visualModel.limitation: No new near-star speed path was added because it would be a separate dynamic writer and CPU architecture change. Motion-depth acceptance therefore remains an owner-smoke decision.

cpu.classification: MEASURED instruction-exact on the current linked NMOS-6502 routine
cpu.measurementMethod: The relocated STARFIELD binary was loaded at its linked run address and generate_baked_far_star_row was executed to RTS with blank, one-near-collision, corridor, full-width and double-star fixtures.
cpu.legalWorstReason: The base generator introduces at most one near star before far generation, so the synthetic two-collision fixture is not a legal runtime row.
cpu.gate: PASS: the hard requested recovery gate is met; the prior 150-cycle estimate is exceeded only by the double-star collision worst case.

writerSites.mechanicalBaseRowAccess: One bounded occupancy/write path is nested in existing base-row construction and executes before later character layers; it is not an independent late far-star writer.

ringWrap.note: Final visual artifact judgement remains assigned to owner smoke; structural host tests and native cold boot do not replace that judgement.

notes: The one pattern phase byte reuses the former far-phase address.
Three scalar compatibility bytes remain reserved so downstream reviewed state addresses do not move.
The existing 24 bytes of far glyph art remain in the shared 48-byte star glyph bank.
No full shadow screen, BASIC RAM, loader change or new transport record was introduced.
